source_architecture_summary: Two memoir-like passages use sensory descriptions of workplaces to explain vocation: one reflects backward through accumulated memory, while the other captures a first recognition of belonging.
feasibility_notes: Both blueprints replace newspaper work, ink, offices, reporters, and every source anecdote while preserving opportunities to compare sensory detail, tone, and vocational identity.

blueprints.blueprint_focus: Two narrators reconsider how ordinary objects preserve human stories: one sorts belongings after a flood, while another follows the changing life of a folded city map.
blueprints.overall_reading_skill_family: Sensory function, tone, vocation inference, and comparison
blueprints.rhetorical_or_narrative_arc: Workplace inventory, skilled worker or process, sensory interpretation, identity realization
blueprints.distinctness_notes: Uses recovery, memory, and circulation of objects; contains no workplace apprenticeship, skilled craft, sensory vocation, or professional identity arc.

blueprints.blueprint_focus: Two narrators learn that demanding public-service work is organized by quiet routines outsiders rarely notice.
blueprints.overall_reading_skill_family: Perspective, understated leadership, structural comparison, and theme
blueprints.rhetorical_or_narrative_arc: Initial surface impression, observation of expert routine, small crisis, revised understanding of the work
blueprints.distinctness_notes: Focuses invisible coordination under pressure, separate from Blueprint A's sensory craft and vocational discovery.
